RetryAfter.description: The whole seconds to wait before trying again, at least 1. Sent with `signingKeyUnconfirmed`.

Cursor.description: The page to continue from, as named in the previous page's `next`.
Cursor.name: cursor

ExternalId.description: The resource's externalId, percent-encoded, matched exactly.
ExternalId.name: externalId

IncludeRetired.description: `true` lists retired resources too, and `false`, like leaving it out, lists none. Any other value is refused with `400`. A principal other than a platform administrator sending `true` is refused with `403` `administratorOnly`.
IncludeRetired.name: includeRetired

IncludeRevoked.description: `true` lists revoked grants too, and `false`, like leaving it out, lists none. Any other value is refused with `400`. A principal other than a platform administrator sending `true` is refused with `403` `administratorOnly`.
IncludeRevoked.name: includeRevoked

ListingLimit.description: The most entries on a page. A page size that is no whole number is refused with `400`, and one of zero or below it with `422`.
ListingLimit.name: limit

NoticeVersions.description: The notice versions read by the bridge, comma-separated. A request without it, or listing no version served by the controller, is refused with `406`.
NoticeVersions.name: Usher-Notice-Versions

BodyTooLarge.description: The body is larger than 64 KiB; `bodyTooLarge`, its detail naming the limit.

ChangeUnavailable.description: `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot take the operation now, because it cannot be reached or the instance's database role may only read; nothing of it is written. `outcomeUnknown`: the store did not confirm whether the change was made; read what it changes before trying again. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed.

ChannelAssertionRefused.description: The channel assertion is missing or refused. An unknown application, an application holding no live key, and an assertion verified by no live key receive this one answer; `channelAssertionRefused`.

CredentialRefused.description: No `Authorization` header, or a `Bearer` access token that is refused; `credentialRefused`. Every refused credential receives this one answer. An `Authorization` header in any other form is refused with `400`.

CursorGone.description: The cursor can no longer be answered, `cursorGone`: history it needs is trimmed, it belongs to another epoch, it is ahead of the newest notice, its position now holds a notice other than the one it was issued for, as after a restore, or it cannot be read. Answered before any byte of a stream. The bridge drops every cached entry and polls from head.

InternalError.description: The controller failed to answer the request, and nothing of it was written; `internalError`.

JsonOnly.description: The body is in a media type other than `application/json`, or in none; `unsupportedMediaType`.

MergePatchOnly.description: The body is in a media type other than `application/merge-patch+json`, or in none; `unsupportedMediaType`.

NoticeVersionUnserved.description: The notice versions header is missing or lists no version served by the controller; `noticeVersionUnserved`.

ReadUnavailable.description: `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot be read.

Unreadable.description: The request is unreadable by its shape. `malformedCredential`: an `Authorization` header holding other than exactly one `Bearer` credential, or a credential in the query. `unreadablePath`: a path holding a percent-encoding that is not UTF-8. `unreadableQuery`: a query parameter not taken by the operation, or a value of one it cannot read. `unreadableBody`: a body that is not one JSON object, names a member twice, holds a `__proto__` member, lacks a required member, holds a member of the wrong type, or holds a member not taken by the operation, other than those named in its `422`. `unrepresentableText`: text in the body, or the access token's `sub` or `sid`, holding a NUL character or an unpaired surrogate, neither of which can be stored.

AccessLevel.description: A resource's base tier. An `open` resource's unmarked records reach everyone through the baseline, the anonymous visitor included. A `registered` resource's unmarked records reach every signed-in principal through the signed-in rule. A `grant` resource is reached through a grant alone.

email.description: The address, matched exactly in any letter case. An address not in the form of an address is refused with `422`.

keys.description: Every key issued to the application, in order of `issuedAt`.

ApplicationId.description: An application's id, a generated uuid. It is the application's audience: the `aud` of its Usher tokens and the `iss` of its bridge's channel assertions.

ApplicationKey.description: An application key, never with its value. A key is live from `issuedAt` until `revokedAt`.

confirmedAt.description: When the first exchange verified with the key was answered; `null` until then.

reason.description: `rotated`, `compromised` or `retired`; any other value is refused with `422`. `compromised` records the revocation at `critical`.

description.description: What the application is for. Stored trimmed, and as `null` when empty once trimmed.

displayName.description: The label shown to people in place of the id, stored trimmed and normalized to NFC, and never checked for uniqueness or matched. A display name empty once trimmed, or longer than 128 characters once normalized to NFC, is refused with `422`.

AuditEvent.description: One event as it was written: a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, its severity among its attributes and its fields in `data`. Every instant in it is RFC 3339 in UTC, with `Z`.

type.description: The event type, prefixed `bio.overture.`, such as `bio.overture.grant.creation`.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; `null` or left out on the last.

name.description: The name alone, without its scope: `controlled`, registered as `global.controlled`.

CategoryUpdate.description: A JSON Merge Patch: `null` clears the description. Naming `name` is refused with `422`.

Decision.description: A grant's latest answer: what was decided, when, and what the holder was shown.

capabilities.description: The capabilities shown to the holder.

EgoExport.description: EGO's policies with their group and user permissions, its groups and their members, its users, and the studies holding data, so the controller reads no data and holds no EGO credential.

studiesHoldingData.description: The ids of the studies holding data. A study outside the allowed set is reported when listed here and skipped otherwise.

studyDetails.description: Details for some studies, each study at most once.

members.description: Its members, by EGO user id.

apply.description: Sent as `true` for a real run; a run is dry otherwise.

audiences.description: The applications serving each resource registered by the run, by id. An empty list is refused with `422` `migrationNeedsAnAudience`, and an id naming no registered application with `422` `unknownApplication`.

name.description: The name from which a configured prefix reads a study's id.

fields.description: Values by resource field name. A value for a field not defined by the instance is reported, never written.

id.description: EGO's own id for the user.

providerSubjectId.description: The user's id at the provider they sign in through. For a Keycloak user it is the subject, trusted once the configured realm's directory finds it; a value in the form of an address is read as an address.

status.description: `APPROVED`, `DISABLED`, `PENDING` or `REJECTED`. An approved user's `WRITE` alone migrates.

ExchangeRequest.description: A member other than these two is ignored.

credential.description: The principal's sign-in token from the identity provider. Left out for the anonymous visitor's exchange.

payloadVersions.description: The payload versions read by the bridge.

ExternalId.description: A resource's external identifier: the value naming it in its catalogue.

confirm.description: `true`; any other value is refused with `422`.

reason.description: `credentialCompromise`, `keyCompromise` or `securityIncident`; any other value is refused with `422`.

capabilities.description: What the grant would let its holder use; in a principal's listing of their own grants.

category.description: The scoped record category; `null` for a grant on the whole resource.

expiresAt.description: `null` for a grant that never expires.

selfGrant.description: `true` for a principal's grant to themself.

GrantChange.description: A JSON Merge Patch naming the expiry, the role, or both.

expiresAt.description: The new expiry, an RFC 3339 instant with an offset, or `null` for none. Any other string is refused with `422`.

role.description: A role defined by the instance; any other is refused with `422`.

category.description: A scoped record category, such as `global.controlled`. Left out of an owner grant, and of a submitter grant taking the instance's submitter category.

expiresAt.description: When the grant ends: an RFC 3339 instant with an offset, `Z` or `±hh:mm`. The grant never expires when it is left out. Any other string is refused with `422`.

role.description: A role defined by the instance; any other is refused with `422`.

capabilities.description: The capabilities shown to the holder.

decision.description: `accepted` or `rejected`; any other string is refused with `422`.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; `null` or left out on the last.

reason.description: `accessNoLongerNeeded`, `accessReview`, `custodianRequest`, `grantedInError`, `holderLeftProject`, `requestedByHolder` or `termsViolation`; any other value is refused with `422`.

GrantState.description: A grant's state, from its expiry, its revocation and its latest decision.

Holder.description: A grant's holder: exactly one person, by `subject` or by `email`. An address is resolved through the directory and never stored. Any other holder, a group or one naming both included, is refused with `422`.

email.description: The address held by the directory, read when the answer is written and never stored; left out for an account no longer known to the directory.

Instant.description: An RFC 3339 instant in UTC, written with `Z`.

value.description: The key: 32 bytes as 43 base64url characters, for the application's bridge.

MemberReason.description: Why a member was written nothing.

MemberResolution.description: How a member's account was sought at the identity provider.

MigrationReport.description: What a run did, or would do. A dry run and a real run on the same data report the same items, `dryRun` apart.

allStudyAccess.description: Every holding of a policy named by the configuration as granting every study. No grant is written for one.

group.description: The group through which the policy is held; `null` for the user's own permission.

caseOnlyMatches.description: Policies matched by a configured prefix only when letter case is ignored. The run leaves them alone.

dataWithoutPolicy.description: The studies holding data whose id is read by no configured prefix from any policy's name. Nothing is registered for them.

resourcesWithoutOwner.description: By externalId, each resource registered without an owner: by this run, or, for a dry run, by a real run on the same data.

unmatchedPolicies.description: Policies matched by no configured prefix in any letter case.

NamedPrincipal.description: How an answer names a principal: by subject to a platform administrator, and in the answer to the principal's own act; by name in a listing to anyone else.

subject.description: The identity provider's subject, the `sub` claim.

reason.description: `accountClosed`, `credentialCompromise`, `securityIncident` or `termsViolation`; any other value is refused with `422`.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem details. `code` names the refusal. No member repeats a value the request carried.

members.description: Every member of the study's groups, each once.

address.description: The address given by the export, as written; `null` where EGO holds none.

addressDiffers.description: Whether the member was found by subject while the account found holds an address other than EGO's.

policies.description: The policies of the study under which the member was found.

reason.description: Why the member was written nothing; `null` for a member written the submitter grant.

missingFromSomeGroups.description: Members missing from some of the study's groups, each granted all the same.

otherReadings.description: The ids read from the same policy name by another configured prefix.

outcome.description: `registered` for a resource registered for the study, `existing` for a resource already held by Usher, `reported` for a study not migrated that holds data or breaks a rule, and `skipped` for one outside the allowed set holding none.

reasons.description: Why the study was reported or skipped: every rule broken by its id, in a fixed order, then any other reason. Empty for one registered or existing.

undefinedFields.description: Values given by its details for resource fields not defined by the instance, each reported and none written.

applications.description: The applications serving the resource, by id.

fields.description: Values by resource field name. A cleared value is left out.

grantSummary.description: How many principals hold each role, counting accepted, unexpired, unrevoked grants alone. Given to platform administrators and the resource's owners.

grants.description: Its grants, holders included, in a listing entry.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; `null` or left out on the last.

accessLevel.description: `open`, `registered` or `grant`, the instance's default when left out. Any other string is refused with `422`.

applications.description: The applications serving the resource from registration on, by id. An id naming no registered application is refused with `422` `unknownApplication`.

description.description: At most 4096 characters once normalized to NFC; a longer one is refused with `422`.

displayName.description: Not blank, and at most 256 characters once normalized to NFC; any other is refused with `422`.

fields.description: Values by resource field name. A value for a field not defined by the instance is refused with `422`.

owners.description: Its first owners, written as owner grants with the registration.

reason.description: `credentialCompromise`, `custodianRequest`, `keyCompromise` or `securityIncident`; any other value is refused with `422`.

ResourceUpdate.description: A JSON Merge Patch: a member left out keeps its value. Naming `externalId` is refused with `422`.

accessLevel.description: `open`, `registered` or `grant`. `null` and any other string are refused with `422`.

description.description: At most 4096 characters once normalized to NFC, or `null` to clear it; a longer one is refused with `422`.

displayName.description: Not blank, and at most 256 characters once normalized to NFC. `null`, a blank name and a longer one are refused with `422`.

fields.description: Values set, or cleared with `null`, by resource field name. A field not defined by the instance is refused with `422`.

reason.description: `custodianRequest` or `issueResolved`; any other value is refused with `422`.

capabilities.description: Every capability carried by the role afterwards, as `entity.action`.

ScopedCategoryName.description: A category name with its scope: `global.` and a name.

expiresAt.description: When the self-grant ends: an RFC 3339 instant with an offset, in the future and within the instance's longest self-grant life. Any other string is refused with `422`.

role.description: A data-plane role defined by the instance; any other is refused with `422`.

reason.description: `consentWithdrawn`, `custodianRequest`, `dataQualityIssue`, `legalRequest` or `securityIncident`; any other value is refused with `422`.

channelAssertion.description: A channel assertion: a JWT signed by the bridge with HS256 under the channel-assertion subkey of its application key, typed `usher-channel+jwt`, naming its application's id in `iss` and `usher:controller` in `aud`, living at most 60 seconds, with a `jti`. One assertion serves every exchange and every poll made within its lifetime, and is presented to the stream route once at most: a second presentation there is refused `401`, whatever else the request carries. When an application holds two live keys, the controller checks the assertion against each and answers under the key that verified it, for tokens and notices alike.

managementToken.description: An access token from the identity provider, naming the management API's configured audience in `aud` and a configured management client in `azp`. A principal holding the configured administrator realm role, read from each request's token, is a platform administrator. A service account's token is refused on every operation with `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

info.description:
The Usher Controller's HTTP API.

A bridge calls the token exchange and the revocation channel under a channel assertion. A principal calls the management API, under `/admin`, with an access token from the identity provider. The identity provider's sign-out relay and the health checks carry no credential of their own.

Every refusal from the management API is RFC 9457 problem details, `application/problem+json`, carrying a `code` and repeating no value the request carried. A `2XX` answer is a success of any status from 200 to 299. At the token exchange and the revocation channel, every refusal of one status is identical to every other refusal of that status.

A request schema states only what is refused with `400`: each member's type and the required members. Each operation's `422` names the rules it applies beyond them, and which members it refuses with `422` rather than `400`.
info.title: Usher Controller API

post.description:
Registers an application and issues its first key, for platform administrators.

The application's `id` is a generated uuid and is its audience: the `aud` carried by its Usher tokens, and the `iss` of its bridge's channel assertions.

`displayName` is stored trimmed and normalized to NFC, the form whose length is counted. `description` is stored trimmed, and a description that is empty once trimmed is stored as `null`. `displayName` is the label shown to people. It is never matched against anything, so two applications may share one.

The key's `value` is in this answer alone. The controller stores it encrypted and never shows it again.

The audit events `application.registration` and then `applicationKey.issuance` record the registration.

requestBody.description: The application. A member other than these two is refused with `400`.

201.description: The application is registered, with its first key.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

422.description: `displayNameBlank`: `displayName` is empty once trimmed. `displayNameTooLong`: `displayName` is longer than 128 characters once normalized to NFC.

get.description:
Reads an application and every key it was issued, for platform administrators.

Keys are listed in order of `issuedAt`. A time or a principal not set is `null`. No answer holds a key's value.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

404.description: The id names no registered application, or is malformed; `applicationNotFound` for both.

post.description:
Issues another key for an application, for platform administrators, so the application's replicas can move to it while the key they hold stays live. The request carries no body.

An application holds at most two live keys. A third is refused with `applicationKeyLimit` until one of the two live keys is revoked. The key's `value` is in this answer alone.

The audit event `applicationKey.issuance` records the issue.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

404.description: The id names no registered application, or is malformed; `applicationNotFound` for both.

409.description: The application holds two live keys already; `applicationKeyLimit`.

delete.description:
Revokes one of an application's keys, for platform administrators. Once every controller instance has reloaded its keys, each refuses an exchange or a channel request whose channel assertion is verified only by that key.

The body is sent only with a reason: `rotated`, `compromised` or `retired`.

A key revoked already keeps its first revocation, and a second is refused with `doesNotHold`.

The audit event `applicationKey.revocation` records the revocation, at `critical` for the reason `compromised` and at `info` otherwise.

requestBody.description: The reason, sent only when one is given.

200.description: The key is revoked. The answer names the key, who revoked it and when, and never its value.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

404.description: `applicationNotFound` for an application id that is unknown or malformed. `applicationKeyNotFound` for a key id that is unknown or malformed, or names a key of another application.

422.description: The reason is not `rotated`, `compromised` or `retired`; `unknownRevocationReason`.

get.description:
Reads the audit log, for platform administrators, a page at a time: every stored event exactly as it was written, in order of `time` and then of `id`.

Each filter narrows the events, and a filter value is matched literally, its wildcard characters included. `from` is inclusive and `to` exclusive, and an instant written with any offset is read as the same instant in UTC.

The audit event `audit.read` records each read.

parameters.description: A full event type, such as `bio.overture.grant.creation`.
parameters.name: type

parameters.description: The earliest `time`, inclusive: an RFC 3339 instant with an offset.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: The latest `time`, exclusive: an RFC 3339 instant with an offset.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: The most events on a page, from 1 to the maximum; any other size is refused with `400`.
parameters.name: limit

400.description: The request is unreadable by its shape: an `Authorization` header holding other than exactly one `Bearer` credential, or a credential in the query; a query parameter not taken by the operation, or a value of one it cannot read; or a body that is not one JSON object, names a member twice, holds a `__proto__` member, lacks a required member, holds a member of the wrong type, or holds a member not taken by the operation, other than those named in its `422`. A page size of zero, below it, or above the maximum is refused with `400` too.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

get.description: Lists every global category, to platform administrators and to principals owning a resource.

403.description: The principal neither administers the platform nor owns a resource; `ownersAndAdministratorsOnly`. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

post.description:
Registers a global category by its name alone, for platform administrators: `controlled` is answered as `global.controlled`.

A name holds letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, and no scope separator. Every category registered here is global.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

409.description: A global category of that name exists; `alreadyExists`.

422.description: The name is empty, holds a character outside letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, or is not admitted by the payload contract.

2XX.description: The category is registered; `name` carries its scope.

patch.description: Updates a category's description as a JSON Merge Patch, for platform administrators. `null` clears it. The name stays as registered.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

422.description: The update names a member it may not set, such as `name`.

post.description:
Creates a grant: a role on a resource for a holder, named by subject or by address. A holder named by address is found through the identity provider's directory, by exact address in any letter case, and the address is never stored. An owner naming the holder by address receives the same answer whether or not an account holds the address.

A data-plane role names a record category offered by the resource. A control-plane role, such as `owner`, names none and takes the whole resource, and an owner grant takes no expiry. A `submitter` grant naming no category takes the instance's submitter category.

A resource's owners grant access to it. A platform administrator grants the `submitter` and `owner` roles on any resource and makes anyone but themself an owner. No one grants the administrator role.

The holder answers the grant through its decisions. When the instance accepts grants at creation, the controller records the holder's acceptance with the grant.

403.description: `noAuthorityOnResource`: the principal may see the resource and holds no authority to grant on it. `administratorGrantsNoConsumerAccess`: a platform administrator grants access that is the owners' to grant, answered alike whether or not the resource exists. `administratorSelfOwnership`: a platform administrator names themself an owner. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls.

404.description: `resourceNotFound`: no resource holds the externalId, or the principal may not see the one that does. `holderNotFound`, to a platform administrator: no single account holds the address verified, whether no account holds it, the account holding it has not verified it, or several accounts hold it.

409.description: The holder already holds this grant live; `alreadyHolds`.

422.description: A rule is broken. `ownerGrantsDoNotExpire` names an owner grant given an expiry. The rest carry unnamed codes: a role not defined by the instance; a category not offered by the resource; a data-plane role naming no category, or a control-plane role naming one; a field category; a `holder` naming other than exactly one person, by subject or by address; an address not in the form of an address; a `grantedBy`; an expiry that is no RFC 3339 instant with an offset, or one in the past; and the principal naming themself, the text then naming the self-grant operation, `/admin/grants/self`.

503.description: `directoryUnavailable`: a holder named by address while the directory cannot answer. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot take the operation now, because it cannot be reached or the instance's database role may only read; nothing of it is written. `outcomeUnknown`: the store did not confirm whether the change was made; read what it changes before trying again. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed.

2XX.description: The grant is created. `id` is its opaque id.

post.description:
Creates the principal's own grant, which is also its acceptance: a data-plane role on a resource where they hold grant authority, a platform administrator on any resource. The expiry is required, in the future, and within the instance's longest self-grant life.

Each owner of the resource is told of the self-grant.

403.description: `noAuthorityOnResource`: the principal may see the resource and holds no authority to grant on it. `administratorSelfOwnership`: a platform administrator names the `owner` role. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls.

404.description: No resource holds the externalId, or the principal may not see the one that does; `resourceNotFound` either way.

409.description: The principal already holds this grant live; `alreadyHolds`.

422.description: A rule is broken: an expiry in the past or past the longest self-grant life, a control-plane role, or a member naming a holder.

2XX.description: The self-grant is created, with its acceptance.

delete.description:
Revokes a grant, whether pending, accepted, declined or expired.

The body is sent only with a reason. Without one, the controller records `unspecified`, a reason it alone assigns and refuses from anyone else.

A grant revoked already keeps its first revocation, and a second is refused with `doesNotHold`. A resource keeps at least one owner, so revoking its last live owner grant is refused with `resourceNeedsAnOwner`.

`DELETE /admin/grants/`, naming no id, is answered `404` `grantNotFound` too.

requestBody.description: The reason, sent only when one is given.

403.description: A service account calls; `serviceAccountNotPermitted`, before any lookup.

404.description: The id is unknown or malformed, or names a grant on a resource where the principal holds no authority for the operation; `grantNotFound` for each.

409.description: `doesNotHold`: the grant is revoked already. `resourceNeedsAnOwner`: the grant is its resource's last live owner grant, the text saying to add another owner first.

422.description: The reason is outside the grant revocation reasons open to a principal.

2XX.description: The grant is revoked. The answer names its holder, its resource, who revoked it and when.

patch.description: Changes a grant's expiry, or removes it with `null`, or changes its role, as a JSON Merge Patch. A principal notice names the holder.

403.description: A service account calls; `serviceAccountNotPermitted`, before any lookup.

404.description: The id is unknown or malformed, or names a grant on a resource where the principal holds no authority for the operation; `grantNotFound` for each.

422.description: A rule is broken. `ownerGrantsDoNotExpire` names an expiry on an owner grant. An expiry that is no RFC 3339 instant with an offset, or one in the past, and a role not defined by the instance carry unnamed codes.

post.description:
Records the holder's answer to a grant, `accepted` or `rejected`, with the capabilities shown to them, which are those conferred by the grant's role as it stands. Answers are appended, and the latest is current. The grant itself is left unchanged.

Only the grant's holder answers it; anyone else receives `grantNotFound`. An owner declining their resource's last live owner grant is refused with `resourceNeedsAnOwner`.

403.description: A service account calls; `serviceAccountNotPermitted`, before any lookup.

404.description: The id is unknown or malformed, or the principal is not the grant's holder; `grantNotFound` for each.

409.description: `doesNotHold`: the grant is revoked or expired. `resourceNeedsAnOwner`: the answer declines a resource's last live owner grant, the text saying to add another owner first.

422.description: The decision is neither `accepted` nor `rejected`, or the capabilities differ from those conferred by the role.

get.description: Lists the principal's own grants, a page at a time, pending ones included and revoked ones left out. Each carries the capabilities it would let them use, and names its granter by name. Any signed-in principal lists their own; one holding nothing receives an empty list.

403.description: `administratorOnly`: a principal other than a platform administrator asks for revoked grants. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls.

422.description: The page size is zero or below it.

503.description: `directoryUnavailable`: the directory cannot answer, for a listing naming a granter. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot be read.

2XX.description: A page of the principal's grants.

post.description:
Migrates EGO's study groups from an export, for platform administrators. The administrator is checked before the body is read, and the body may be up to 10 MiB.

A run is dry unless `apply: true` is sent beside the export. A dry run writes nothing and reports exactly what a real run on the same data then does. A real run writes all of its changes or none of them, and holds a lock that refuses a second run until it ends.

Each resource registered by a run takes the instance's configured base tier and is served by every application named in `audiences`. The prefixes that read a study's id from a policy's name, and the policies granting every study, come from the instance's configuration.

Either run answers its report to the administrator alone. The report is never written to the log stream.

403.description: The principal is no platform administrator; `administratorOnly`, before any lookup, so the answer is the same whether or not the thing named exists. A service account receives `serviceAccountNotPermitted`.

413.description: The body is larger than 10 MiB; `bodyTooLarge`, its detail naming the limit.

422.description: `unknownApplication`: `audiences` names an application that is not registered. `migrationNeedsAnAudience`: `audiences` is empty.

503.description: `migrationNotConfigured`: a setting read by the migration from the instance's configuration is missing, checked before the export is read. `directoryUnavailable`: the directory cannot answer a lookup during the run. `storeUnavailable`: the store cannot complete the run, and nothing of it is written. `outcomeUnknown`: the store did not confirm whether the change was made; read what it changes before trying again. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed.

post.description:
Lists, a page at a time, the grants of the principal holding an address. The principal is found by exact address in any letter case, the address in the body.

A platform administrator receives every grant across resources, and a resource's owner the grants on resources they own. Revoked grants are listed only to an administrator asking with `includeRevoked=true`.

To a platform administrator, an address held by no single account is refused with `holderNotFound`. To an owner, it is answered as an account holding nothing on their resources.

403.description: `administratorOnly`: a principal other than a platform administrator asks for revoked grants. `serviceAccountNotPermitted`: a service account calls.

404.description: To a platform administrator, no single account holds the address; `holderNotFound`.

422.description: The address is not in the form of an address, or the page size is zero or below it.

503.description: `directoryUnavailable`: the directory cannot answer. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the identity provider's signing keys cannot be fetched to verify the access token, or the token's signing key is not among those held while the latest fetch of them has failed. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the access token's signing key is not among those held, and the keys were fetched too recently to fetch them again; try again once the seconds in `Retry-After` have passed. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot be read.

post.description:
Revokes a principal entirely, by subject, for platform administrators. While the revocation stands, the exchange refuses the principal's every credential at every audience, and their grants are kept.

A principal notice names them to every application, and the audit event `identity.revocation` records the revocation.

422.description: The reason is not one of the identity revocation reasons.

post.description:
Lifts a principal's standing revocation, by subject, for platform administrators, keeping its history. The exchange issues them tokens again, from the grants they held throughout.

A principal notice names them to every application, and the audit event `identity.revocationLift` records the lift.

post.description:
Registers a resource under its externalId, for platform administrators.

`accessLevel` takes the instance's default when left out. `applications` names every application serving the resource from registration on, and each must be registered. `owners` names its first owners, written as owner grants in the registration's transaction; a platform administrator never names themself. Each value in `fields` names a resource field defined by the instance.

An externalId is in Unicode normalization form C, and from 1 to 128 characters long. It starts with a letter or a digit and holds letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, or the wider set configured for the instance, never a filter marker, and is never `__proto__`. One externalId names one resource in any letter case, a retired resource included.

409.description: A resource holds the externalId in some letter case, a retired one included; `alreadyExists`.

422.description: A rule is broken. `unknownApplication` names an application that is not registered, refusing the whole registration. The rest carry unnamed codes: an externalId breaking a rule of its form, NFC included; a display name that is blank or longer than 256 characters; a description longer than 4096 characters; an access level other than `open`, `registered` and `grant`; and a value for a field not defined by the instance.

post.description:
The identity provider's OpenID Connect back-channel logout endpoint. The body is form-encoded and holds one `logout_token`: a current logout token issued by the configured identity provider for the instance's back-channel logout clients alone, naming a session in `sid`, a subject in `sub`, or both. The header `typ` is `logout+jwt` or `JWT`, in any letter case and with or without the `application/` prefix, or left out.

The controller commits the sign-out, with a principal notice to every application where the subject is known, before it answers. The exchange then refuses every sign-in token of a session named by the logout token, whenever it was issued. For a logout token naming a subject alone, the exchange refuses each of that subject's sign-in tokens issued before the sign-out.

A logout token delivered twice writes one notice. A logout naming a session unseen at any exchange writes no notice, and the sign-in tokens of that session are refused all the same.

400.description: The logout is not taken, and its code names why, as Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.8 has every logout not taken answered `400`. `unreadableQuery`: the request carries a query, so a logout token is never read from a URL. `bodyTooLarge`: the body is larger than 64 KiB. `unreadableBody`: the body is not `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` in UTF-8 holding exactly one non-empty `logout_token`. `logoutTokenRefused`: the token is not a current logout token issued by the configured identity provider, signed by one of its published keys, for the instance's back-channel logout clients alone, naming a session in `sid`, a subject in `sub`, or both. A logout token carries `events` holding the back-channel logout member as a JSON object, and no `nonce`, whatever its `typ`. Its `aud` names at least one configured back-channel logout client and no other audience. It is current when its `iat` is ahead of the controller's clock by less than the clock tolerance and no older than the longest sign-in token lifetime the instance accepts, and its `exp` has not passed. Every refusal of a token is answered alike. `identityProviderUnavailable`: the token's signing key is not among the keys fetched by the controller, while the identity provider cannot be reached. `signingKeyUnconfirmed`: the token's signing key is not among the keys fetched by the controller, and the refetch cooldown since a fetch that succeeded forbids fetching them again yet; a key the provider published since, as by a rotation, is found by the next fetch, so the logout token may be sent again later. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot take the sign-out now, because it cannot be reached or the instance's database role may only read; nothing of it is written. `outcomeUnknown`: the store did not confirm whether the sign-out was recorded; the logout token may be sent again, since a sign-out recorded already writes nothing more. `internalError`: the controller failed to take the logout, and nothing of it was written.

post.summary: Relays a sign-out from the identity provider

post.description:
Answers an Usher token for the channel assertion's application, whatever the body carries: the anonymous visitor's for a body carrying no `credential`, or the principal's for a sign-in token verified by the identity provider's realm.

The token is a compact JWE whose protected header holds `alg` `dir`, `enc` `A256GCM` and `typ` `usher+jwt` alone, encrypted under the token subkey of the application key that verified the channel assertion. Its payload is in the highest version listed by the request and served by the controller.

The first exchange verified with a key records the key's `confirmedAt`, and the audit event `applicationKey.confirmation` records it once.

The channel assertion is checked first, so an exchange whose assertion is refused does no other work. A body member other than `credential` and `payloadVersions` is ignored.

schema.description: The Usher token, a compact JWE.

200.description: The Usher token, alone, as the body.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, `payloadVersions` is missing, empty or holds anything but positive whole numbers, or `credential` is not a string.

401.description: The channel assertion is missing or refused. An unknown application, an application holding no live key, and an assertion verified by no live key receive this one answer.

403.description: The credential is refused. Every refused credential, a revoked principal's included, receives this one answer, with the same body.

406.description: `payloadVersions` lists no version served by the controller.

413.description: The body is larger than 64 KiB.

503.description: The identity provider's realm or the policy store cannot be reached, a principal's first exchange cannot record their identity, or the token would be larger than the bridge's response cap. No token is issued.

post.summary: Exchanges a credential for an Usher token

get.description: Answers `200` while the process runs and its log stream has taken every line, and `503` once a write to the log stream has failed, neither with any detail in the body. The stream takes nothing more after a failed write, and only a restart recovers the instance. No credential is needed.

200.description: The process runs, and its log stream has taken every line.

503.description: A write to the log stream has failed. Restart the instance.

get.description: Answers `200` while the instance can serve and `503` while it cannot, neither with any detail in the body. No credential is needed.

Answers the notices of the channel assertion's application, from one starting point: `head=true` answers no notices and the cursor of the newest committed notice, and `after` answers the notices after that cursor in position order, a page at a time. A poll is answered at once, from the policy store alone.

The answer is a compact JWE typed `usher-poll+jwt`, encrypted under the poll-answer subkey of the application key that verified the channel assertion. Its plaintext holds exactly `v`, `nonce`, `after`, `notices`, `next` and `more`: the request's nonce and starting point echoed as sent, the notices, the cursor to poll after next, and whether more notices wait. Each notice is in a version listed by the request.

Checks run in this order: the channel assertion, the notice versions, the query, then the cursor.

parameters.description: Asks for no notices and the newest cursor. Sent as `true`, in place of `after`.
parameters.name: head

parameters.description: The cursor after which notices are answered, in place of `head`.
parameters.name: after

parameters.description: A fresh value, echoed in the answer: 16 to 128 base64url characters, unpadded.
parameters.name: nonce

schema.description: The poll answer, a compact JWE.

400.description: The query names no starting point or both, repeats a parameter, holds a `head` other than `true` or an empty `after`, carries no nonce of 16 to 128 base64url characters, or holds a parameter other than `head`, `after` and `nonce`; `unreadableQuery`.

503.description: The policy store cannot be reached; `storeUnavailable`.

get.description:
An event stream of the notices of the channel assertion's application, starting after the cursor in `Last-Event-ID`: every notice committed after it, in position order, then each new one as it commits. The poll and the stream deliver one application's notices in the same order.

Each notice is one event named `notice`, whose `id` is its cursor and whose `data` is a compact JWE typed `usher-notice+jwt`, encrypted under the notice subkey of the application key that verified the channel assertion. Comment lines, which carry no notice, keep the connection open.

The headers and a first byte are sent at once, uncompressed. A stream ends within the instance's configured maximum lifetime, and one channel assertion is presented to it once at most.

parameters.description: The cursor after which the stream starts.
parameters.name: Last-Event-ID

schema.description: Server-sent events, each notice an event named `notice`.

X-Accel-Buffering.description: Holds `no`, so a proxy passes each event on at once.

401.description: The channel assertion is missing or refused, or has been presented to the stream route already, whatever else the request carries; `channelAssertionRefused`, the one answer every refused assertion receives.

503.description: `streamLimitReached`: the application holds as many open streams on this instance as it may. `storeUnavailable`: the policy store cannot be reached. `instanceStopping`: the instance is stopping. A stream is also refused when the instance cannot record the channel assertion as used.
